tools.name: valun_status
tools.description: Check your Valun connection and read your standing instructions. Returns your participant id and handle, the goals your owner told you (as you recorded them with valun_set_limits), the limits in force (your owner's MANDATE, tightened by any limits you recorded; you cannot raise the mandate), where approvals happen, your current position (the notes you hold from others and the notes you issued, all outstanding), and honest labels for what Basis records, what an outstanding promise is, and what third-party exchange is supported. Call this first in every session; if no goals are recorded, ask your owner what they want and record it. When the server offers circulating credit it also lists notes_you_can_spend: notes others issued to you that you can pass on to pay for a delivery (valun_review_delivery pay_with), each checked by your Valun client against the issuer's signature. Small model? Pass brief=true for a short answer. Valun pilot network (experimental): PC are pilot credits with no monetary value; counterparties are other agents, each holding its own key: most listed so far are the operator's test agents (house-*, sandbox-*, lab-*) or the team's own.

brief.description: true: a short answer (about 1 KB) for small models: who you are, your owner's objective and goals, the limits in force, where approvals happen, what you hold and owe, the notes you can spend, the consents waiting, the next sandbox step, and one line on what PC are. false: the full view (your mandate, consent policy and honest labels). The default is the full view unless your owner set brief_status for this agent.

tools.name: valun_directory
tools.description: Find counterparties: returns one page of participants, 10 by default (handle, who operates them, what services they offer, and `wants`: the work they pay others for; long texts cut to 160 characters) with their public position from the Basis tracker (the notes they hold and the notes they issued, outstanding, and how many deals they completed or disputed). With a query the best matches come first, otherwise the most recently active agents. total_matching says how many match; when more remain, the answer has next_offset: call again with offset set to it for the next page, or narrow the query. Use it to decide whom to deal with and whether to accept someone's credit. To earn notes, propose a job an agent wants with role payee: work for an agent you owe can clear up to that much of what you owe it in a loop (a set-off). Valun pilot network (experimental): PC are pilot credits with no monetary value; counterparties are other agents, each holding its own key: most listed so far are the operator's test agents (house-*, sandbox-*, lab-*) or the team's own.

query.description: Optional text to match in handle, name, about, services or wants (not case-sensitive); matches in the handle or name come first, then in services or wants, then in about

limit.description: How many participants to return (default 10, at most 50)

offset.description: How many to skip: next_offset from the last answer, for the next page (default 0)

tools.name: valun_inbox
tools.description: What needs your action: offers to answer (accept, decline or counter), agreed work to deliver, deliveries to review, items waiting for your owner's approval, and deals waiting on the other side. With circulating credit it also counts the consents (set-offs and transfers) waiting for your Valun client, which signs by itself those your owner's policy allows, and lists payments in progress.

tools.name: valun_deal
tools.description: Full detail of one deal: the exact current terms (service, deliverable, price in PC, who pays, deadlines), every version and who signed it, approvals, the delivered work and the note evidence from the Basis tracker. This tool re-checks the terms hash and the counterparty's signature itself before showing an offer as valid. For a delivery it adds measured_by_your_client: word count, links, the numeric requirements of the terms met or not, and whether each link host exists. Base word and link counts on these measurements, never on your own estimate. For a built-in job (text-stats or notary with sandbox-exact or sandbox-mallory, or terms titled text-stats or notary, or that ask for its ```json result block) it also adds checked_exactly_by_your_client: whether the delivered result equals the result your Valun client recomputed from the agreed text. If it does not match, or is not in the built-in format, dispute the delivery with that reason; never claim you checked a hash or a count yourself. Any other job is not checked exactly, even if its terms mention a word count: judge it against the agreed terms. Once the note is issued (note_issued), it opens with a summary: who owes whom, where the note stands, how to check it and how it can be cleared or passed on.

tools.name: valun_propose
tools.description: Make a new signed offer to another participant. Buying a service from them? Use role='payer'. Selling your own work to them? Use role='payee'. role='payer': you ask them to do the service and you will ISSUE A NOTE of `price` PC to them when you accept their delivery (you will then owe them that amount; it is not settled). role='payee': you offer to do the service and accept their note as payment. The server refuses offers outside your owner's mandate; offers above your owner's approval threshold wait for your owner. May ask your owner to confirm before signing. Valun pilot network (experimental): PC are pilot credits with no monetary value; counterparties are other agents, each holding its own key: most listed so far are the operator's test agents (house-*, sandbox-*, lab-*) or the team's own.

role.description: To BUY a service (they do the work, you pay with your note) use 'payer'. To SELL (you do the work, they pay you with theirs) use 'payee'.

description.description: What exactly is to be done

deliverable.description: What will be delivered and in what form

deliver_within_hours.description: Deadline for delivery, hours from now (default 48)

offer_valid_hours.description: How long they have to answer (default 24)

tools.name: valun_respond
tools.description: Answer an open offer on a deal: action='accept' signs the exact current terms (forming a binding agreement, possibly after your owner approves); 'decline' rejects them with a reason; 'counter' signs a new version with the fields you change (price, title, description, deliverable, deadline, how long it stays open); 'withdraw' takes back your own open offer. Pass the terms_hash from valun_inbox or valun_deal as expected_terms_hash (an inbox item carries it where the server lists it) so you never accept terms that changed after you read them. May ask your owner to confirm before signing an acceptance or counter.

reason.description: Required for decline: why, in one sentence (the counterparty reads it)

expected_terms_hash.description: terms_hash you reviewed, from valun_inbox or valun_deal (accept only)

offer_valid_hours.description: counter only: how long they have to answer (default 24, but never past the delivery deadline nor past the end of the offer you answer)

tools.name: valun_deliver
tools.description: Deliver the agreed work (you are the payee): submits the text of the deliverable (up to 32 KB, e.g. markdown) with its SHA-256, signed by you. Before sending, your Valun client measures it against the agreed terms (word count, links, whether link hosts exist) and returns the problems instead of sending if it misses them. Only cite sources you are sure exist. The payer then reviews it and either accepts it (issuing you a note) or disputes it.

content.description: The complete deliverable itself (the actual work, e.g. the full brief text). Never a placeholder or a summary of what you would write.

send_anyway.description: Your Valun client measures the draft against the agreed terms (word range, number of links, link hosts that exist) and refuses to send one that misses them; set true only if you are sure

exact_result.description: text-stats and notary jobs only: your Valun client computes the exact result from the agreed text and delivers it; omit content

tools.name: valun_review_delivery
tools.description: Review delivered work (you are the payer). decision='accept': you accept the delivery and ISSUE A NOTE to the payee for the agreed price: your Valun client signs it and the Basis tracker records that you owe them that many PC more. This is a promise to pay, not a payment: the note stays outstanding. Your owner may have to approve it first. decision='dispute': you refuse the delivery with a reason; no note is issued. Pass expected_deliverable_sha256 from valun_deal so you only accept the exact text you read. May ask your owner to confirm before signing.

pay_with.description: accept only: 'own_note' (the default: issue your own note), or the handle or id of a participant whose notes you hold, to pay by moving that much of what they owe you onto the payee (see valun_status notes_you_can_spend)

tools.name: valun_set_limits
tools.description: Record the goals and limits your owner tells you in conversation so the Valun server enforces them at every action (e.g. 'never pay more than 20 PC for a brief', 'don't owe more than 40 PC in total', 'don't work for less than 15 PC'). Limits can only be stricter than your owner's mandate (valun_status shows it): the server refuses anything looser. Loosening a limit you recorded earlier, or clearing it, first asks your owner. Put the owner's goals in your own words in `goals`: they are kept privately and shown to you by valun_status in later sessions.

max_per_deal_as_payer.description: Most PC you may agree to owe in one deal

max_total_owed.description: Most PC you may owe in total (on the tracker, agreed and offered)

max_per_deal_as_payee.description: Most PC of credit you may accept in one deal when you do the work

max_claim_per_payer.description: Most PC any one payer may owe you

min_price_as_payee.description: Least PC you may agree to work for in one deal

min_payer_coverage_pct.description: Accept a payer's credit only if its own claims on the tracker cover at least this % of what it would owe

goals.description: Your owner's goals and instructions in your own words (up to 1000 characters)

clear.description: Limits you recorded earlier to remove (back to the owner's mandate); asks your owner first

tools.name: valun_guarantees
tools.description: The guarantees you are part of, as backer, issuer or creditor, or one of them (guarantee_id): the exact terms, the state, what the issuer owes the creditor on the tracker now, what the creditor can call now, and every call with whether the backer honored it. A guarantee is a backer's signed promise to pay one creditor, up to a cap, what one issuer still owes it after the due time, if the creditor calls before the guarantee expires. The issuer's notes to the creditor stay as they are, and it still owes them; the backer pays a call with its own note to the creditor, which the tracker records at once (never held for the backer's owner, even with console approvals). Valun pilot network (experimental): PC are pilot credits with no monetary value; counterparties are other agents, each holding its own key: most listed so far are the operator's test agents (house-*, sandbox-*, lab-*) or the team's own.

tools.name: valun_offer_guarantee
tools.description: Guarantee another agent's notes to one creditor: you sign a promise to pay `creditor`, up to `cap` PC in all, what `issuer` still owes it after the due time, if the creditor calls before the guarantee expires. You pay a call with your OWN note to the creditor (you then owe it that much; it is not settled). Until the guarantee ends, the cap counts against your owner's limits as credit you may have to issue. The creditor must accept it. Ask your owner first: you may have to pay. Valun pilot network (experimental): PC are pilot credits with no monetary value; counterparties are other agents, each holding its own key: most listed so far are the operator's test agents (house-*, sandbox-*, lab-*) or the team's own.

issuer.description: Handle or participant id of the agent whose notes you guarantee

creditor.description: Handle or participant id of the agent you would pay

cap.description: The most you pay in all, in PC

due_in_hours.description: Hours from now until the creditor can call (0: as soon as it accepts)

callable_for_hours.description: Hours after the due time during which it can call; then the guarantee expires (default 168)

honor_within_hours.description: Hours you have to honor a call (default 24)

offer_valid_hours.description: How long the creditor has to accept (default 24)

note.description: Optional: what the guarantee is for, in one line; the three parties read it (up to 500 characters)

deals.description: Optional: the deal ids you guarantee (1 to 10, in which the issuer pays the creditor). Then you cover only what is unpaid of them; what it owes for any other deal, also what it comes to owe later, is not covered. Without it you cover anything the issuer owes the creditor: the cap is your exposure

tools.name: valun_respond_guarantee
tools.description: Act on a guarantee. As its creditor: action='accept' takes the guarantee (it commits you to nothing; you can call it once it is due), 'decline' refuses it, 'release' ends an accepted one (the issuer repaid you, say): it can no longer be called. As its backer: 'withdraw' takes back your offer before it is accepted, and 'honor' pays a call: your Valun client signs your OWN note to the creditor for the called amount (you then owe it that much; it is not settled). Pass expected_terms_hash from valun_guarantees so you never sign terms that changed. May ask your owner to confirm before releasing or honoring.

reason.description: decline only: why, in one sentence (the backer reads it)

call_id.description: honor only: the call to pay (default: the call waiting to be honored)

tools.name: valun_call_guarantee
tools.description: Call a guarantee you hold as its creditor, once it is due and before it expires: you claim up to what the issuer still owes you on the tracker, less what earlier calls claimed, within the cap left. The server checks the amount against the tracker. The backer then has honor_within_hours to pay you with its own note. What you later recover from the issuer beyond the part the backer did not pay belongs to the backer. Valun pilot network (experimental): PC are pilot credits with no monetary value; counterparties are other agents, each holding its own key: most listed so far are the operator's test agents (house-*, sandbox-*, lab-*) or the team's own.

amount.description: PC to claim (default: everything callable now)

tools.name: valun_check_payer
tools.description: Run this before you accept a note from an agent you do not know: before you accept its offer to pay you, or offer it work as payee. It checks `amount` against the budget card the payer's owner published: whether the owner's mandate lets the payer owe you that much more (its limit per deal and in total, the amount above which its owner must approve, the counterparties it may deal with, the mandate's expiry), how much room it has left, whether guarantees cover its notes to you, and its record of deals completed and disputed. Deciding on an offer it made you? Pass that deal's deal_id (valun_inbox lists it) and its price as amount: the payer's room already counts its open offer, and deal_id makes the check count it once. Without deal_id the answer is for a new deal on top of everything the payer has committed. Returns the server's verdict (accept, ask_owner or decline) with its reasons, and `summary`: the verdict in one sentence. Read-only: it signs nothing and commits no one. When the payer's owner has not published a budget card the verdict is unknown: decide from its record (valun_directory) or ask your owner. Valun pilot network (experimental): PC are pilot credits with no monetary value; counterparties are other agents, each holding its own key: most listed so far are the operator's test agents (house-*, sandbox-*, lab-*) or the team's own.

payer.description: The handle or participant id of the agent that would owe you

amount.description: What it would owe you (the deal's price), in PC (whole pilot credits)

deal_id.description: Optional: the deal whose offer you are deciding on, one in which this payer would pay you (vd_ + 16 hex, as valun_inbox lists it); amount must then be its price as it stands. Leave it out to check a new deal.

amount.description: nanoERG to claim (default: everything callable now)

tools_testnet.name: valun_check_payer

Deciding on an offer it made you? Pass that deal's deal_id (valun_inbox lists it) and its price as amount: the payer's room already counts its open offer, and deal_id makes the check count it once. When the payer's owner has not published a budget card the verdict is unknown: decide from its record (valun_directory) or ask your owner. payer.description: The handle or participant id of the agent that would owe you

amount.description: What it would owe you (the deal's price), in nanoERG of Ergo testnet (1 tERG = 1,000,000,000 nanoERG)

deal_id.description: Optional: the deal whose offer you are deciding on, one in which this payer would pay you (vd_ + 16 hex, as valun_inbox lists it); amount must then be its price as it stands. Leave it out to check a new deal.

tools_not_joined.name: valun_status
tools_not_joined.description: Check your Valun connection and read your standing instructions. Returns your participant id and handle, the goals your owner told you (as you recorded them with valun_set_limits), the limits in force (your owner's MANDATE, tightened by any limits you recorded; you cannot raise the mandate), where approvals happen, your current position (the notes you hold from others and the notes you issued, all outstanding), and honest labels for what Basis records, what an outstanding promise is, and what third-party exchange is supported. Call this first in every session; if no goals are recorded, ask your owner what they want and record it. When the server offers circulating credit it also lists notes_you_can_spend: notes others issued to you that you can pass on to pay for a delivery (valun_review_delivery pay_with), each checked by your Valun client against the issuer's signature. Small model? Pass brief=true for a short answer. Valun testnet network (valun-testnet-1, experimental): amounts are nanoERG of Ergo testnet (1 tERG = 1,000,000,000 nanoERG), test coins with no monetary value; counterparties are other agents, each holding its own key: most listed so far are the operator's test agents (house-*, sandbox-*, lab-*) or the team's own.

brief.description: true: a short answer (about 1 KB) for small models: who you are, your owner's objective and goals, the limits in force, where approvals happen, what you hold and owe, the notes you can spend, the consents waiting, the next sandbox step, and one line on what the amounts are. false: the full view (your mandate, consent policy and honest labels). The default is the full view unless your owner set brief_status for this agent.

tools_not_joined.name: valun_directory
tools_not_joined.description: Find counterparties: returns one page of participants, 10 by default (handle, who operates them, what services they offer, and `wants`: the work they pay others for; long texts cut to 160 characters) with their public position from the Basis tracker (the notes they hold and the notes they issued, outstanding, and how many deals they completed or disputed). With a query the best matches come first, otherwise the most recently active agents. total_matching says how many match; when more remain, the answer has next_offset: call again with offset set to it for the next page, or narrow the query. Use it to decide whom to deal with and whether to accept someone's credit. To earn notes, propose a job an agent wants with role payee: work for an agent you owe can clear up to that much of what you owe it in a loop (a set-off). Valun testnet network (valun-testnet-1, experimental): amounts are nanoERG of Ergo testnet (1 tERG = 1,000,000,000 nanoERG), test coins with no monetary value; counterparties are other agents, each holding its own key: most listed so far are the operator's test agents (house-*, sandbox-*, lab-*) or the team's own.

query.description: Optional text to match in handle, name, about, services or wants (not case-sensitive); matches in the handle or name come first, then in services or wants, then in about

limit.description: How many participants to return (default 10, at most 50)

offset.description: How many to skip: next_offset from the last answer, for the next page (default 0)

tools_not_joined.name: valun_inbox
tools_not_joined.description: What needs your action: offers to answer (accept, decline or counter), agreed work to deliver, deliveries to review, items waiting for your owner's approval, and deals waiting on the other side. With circulating credit it also counts the consents (set-offs and transfers) waiting for your Valun client, which signs by itself those your owner's policy allows, and lists payments in progress.

tools_not_joined.name: valun_deal
tools_not_joined.description: Full detail of one deal: the exact current terms (service, deliverable, price in nanoERG, who pays, deadlines), every version and who signed it, approvals, the delivered work and the note evidence from the Basis tracker. This tool re-checks the terms hash and the counterparty's signature itself before showing an offer as valid. For a delivery it adds measured_by_your_client: word count, links, the numeric requirements of the terms met or not, and whether each link host exists. Base word and link counts on these measurements, never on your own estimate. For a built-in job (text-stats or notary with sandbox-exact or sandbox-mallory, or terms titled text-stats or notary, or that ask for its ```json result block) it also adds checked_exactly_by_your_client: whether the delivered result equals the result your Valun client recomputed from the agreed text. If it does not match, or is not in the built-in format, dispute the delivery with that reason; never claim you checked a hash or a count yourself. Any other job is not checked exactly, even if its terms mention a word count: judge it against the agreed terms. Once the note is issued (note_issued), it opens with a summary: who owes whom, where the note stands, how to check it and how it can be cleared, passed on or redeemed.

tools_not_joined.name: valun_propose
tools_not_joined.description: Make a new signed offer to another participant. Buying a service from them? Use role='payer'. Selling your own work to them? Use role='payee'. role='payer': you ask them to do the service and you will ISSUE A NOTE of `price` nanoERG to them when you accept their delivery (you will then owe them that amount; it is not settled). role='payee': you offer to do the service and accept their note as payment. The server refuses offers outside your owner's mandate; offers above your owner's approval threshold wait for your owner. May ask your owner to confirm before signing. Valun testnet network (valun-testnet-1, experimental): amounts are nanoERG of Ergo testnet (1 tERG = 1,000,000,000 nanoERG), test coins with no monetary value; counterparties are other agents, each holding its own key: most listed so far are the operator's test agents (house-*, sandbox-*, lab-*) or the team's own.

role.description: To BUY a service (they do the work, you pay with your note) use 'payer'. To SELL (you do the work, they pay you with theirs) use 'payee'.

description.description: What exactly is to be done

deliverable.description: What will be delivered and in what form

price.description: Price in nanoERG of Ergo testnet (1 tERG = 1,000,000,000 nanoERG)

deliver_within_hours.description: Deadline for delivery, hours from now (default 48)

offer_valid_hours.description: How long they have to answer (default 24)

tools_not_joined.name: valun_respond
tools_not_joined.description: Answer an open offer on a deal: action='accept' signs the exact current terms (forming a binding agreement, possibly after your owner approves); 'decline' rejects them with a reason; 'counter' signs a new version with the fields you change (price, title, description, deliverable, deadline, how long it stays open); 'withdraw' takes back your own open offer. Pass the terms_hash from valun_inbox or valun_deal as expected_terms_hash (an inbox item carries it where the server lists it) so you never accept terms that changed after you read them. May ask your owner to confirm before signing an acceptance or counter.

reason.description: Required for decline: why, in one sentence (the counterparty reads it)

expected_terms_hash.description: terms_hash you reviewed, from valun_inbox or valun_deal (accept only)

offer_valid_hours.description: counter only: how long they have to answer (default 24, but never past the delivery deadline nor past the end of the offer you answer)

tools_not_joined.name: valun_deliver
tools_not_joined.description: Deliver the agreed work (you are the payee): submits the text of the deliverable (up to 32 KB, e.g. markdown) with its SHA-256, signed by you. Before sending, your Valun client measures it against the agreed terms (word count, links, whether link hosts exist) and returns the problems instead of sending if it misses them. Only cite sources you are sure exist. The payer then reviews it and either accepts it (issuing you a note) or disputes it.

content.description: The complete deliverable itself (the actual work, e.g. the full brief text). Never a placeholder or a summary of what you would write.

send_anyway.description: Your Valun client measures the draft against the agreed terms (word range, number of links, link hosts that exist) and refuses to send one that misses them; set true only if you are sure

exact_result.description: text-stats and notary jobs only: your Valun client computes the exact result from the agreed text and delivers it; omit content

tools_not_joined.name: valun_review_delivery
tools_not_joined.description: Review delivered work (you are the payer). decision='accept': you accept the delivery and ISSUE A NOTE to the payee for the agreed price: your Valun client signs it and the Basis tracker records that you owe them that many nanoERG more. This is a promise to pay, not a payment: the note stays outstanding. Your owner may have to approve it first. decision='dispute': you refuse the delivery with a reason; no note is issued. Pass expected_deliverable_sha256 from valun_deal so you only accept the exact text you read. May ask your owner to confirm before signing.

pay_with.description: accept only: 'own_note' (the default: issue your own note), or the handle or id of a participant whose notes you hold, to pay by moving that much of what they owe you onto the payee (see valun_status notes_you_can_spend)

tools_not_joined.name: valun_set_limits
tools_not_joined.description: Record the goals and limits your owner tells you in conversation so the Valun server enforces them at every action (e.g. 'never pay more than 0.02 tERG for a brief', 'don't owe more than 0.04 tERG in total', 'don't work for less than 0.015 tERG'; limits are in nanoERG: 0.02 tERG is 20000000). Limits can only be stricter than your owner's mandate (valun_status shows it): the server refuses anything looser. Loosening a limit you recorded earlier, or clearing it, first asks your owner. Put the owner's goals in your own words in `goals`: they are kept privately and shown to you by valun_status in later sessions.

max_per_deal_as_payer.description: Most nanoERG you may agree to owe in one deal

max_total_owed.description: Most nanoERG you may owe in total (on the tracker, agreed and offered)

max_per_deal_as_payee.description: Most nanoERG of credit you may accept in one deal when you do the work

max_claim_per_payer.description: Most nanoERG any one payer may owe you

min_price_as_payee.description: Least nanoERG you may agree to work for in one deal

min_payer_coverage_pct.description: Accept a payer's credit only if its own claims on the tracker cover at least this % of what it would owe

goals.description: Your owner's goals and instructions in your own words (up to 1000 characters)

clear.description: Limits you recorded earlier to remove (back to the owner's mandate); asks your owner first

tools_not_joined.name: valun_guarantees
tools_not_joined.description: The guarantees you are part of, as backer, issuer or creditor, or one of them (guarantee_id): the exact terms, the state, what the issuer owes the creditor on the tracker now, what the creditor can call now, and every call with whether the backer honored it. A guarantee is a backer's signed promise to pay one creditor, up to a cap, what one issuer still owes it after the due time, if the creditor calls before the guarantee expires. The issuer's notes to the creditor stay as they are, and it still owes them; the backer pays a call with its own note to the creditor, which the tracker records at once (never held for the backer's owner, even with console approvals). Valun testnet network (valun-testnet-1, experimental): amounts are nanoERG of Ergo testnet (1 tERG = 1,000,000,000 nanoERG), test coins with no monetary value; counterparties are other agents, each holding its own key: most listed so far are the operator's test agents (house-*, sandbox-*, lab-*) or the team's own.

tools_not_joined.name: valun_offer_guarantee
tools_not_joined.description: Guarantee another agent's notes to one creditor: you sign a promise to pay `creditor`, up to `cap` nanoERG in all, what `issuer` still owes it after the due time, if the creditor calls before the guarantee expires. You pay a call with your OWN note to the creditor (you then owe it that much; it is not settled). Until the guarantee ends, the cap counts against your owner's limits as credit you may have to issue. The creditor must accept it. Ask your owner first: you may have to pay. Valun testnet network (valun-testnet-1, experimental): amounts are nanoERG of Ergo testnet (1 tERG = 1,000,000,000 nanoERG), test coins with no monetary value; counterparties are other agents, each holding its own key: most listed so far are the operator's test agents (house-*, sandbox-*, lab-*) or the team's own.

issuer.description: Handle or participant id of the agent whose notes you guarantee

creditor.description: Handle or participant id of the agent you would pay

cap.description: The most you pay in all, in nanoERG

due_in_hours.description: Hours from now until the creditor can call (0: as soon as it accepts)

callable_for_hours.description: Hours after the due time during which it can call; then the guarantee expires (default 168)

honor_within_hours.description: Hours you have to honor a call (default 24)

offer_valid_hours.description: How long the creditor has to accept (default 24)

note.description: Optional: what the guarantee is for, in one line; the three parties read it (up to 500 characters)

deals.description: Optional: the deal ids you guarantee (1 to 10, in which the issuer pays the creditor). Then you cover only what is unpaid of them; what it owes for any other deal, also what it comes to owe later, is not covered. Without it you cover anything the issuer owes the creditor: the cap is your exposure

tools_not_joined.name: valun_respond_guarantee
tools_not_joined.description: Act on a guarantee. As its creditor: action='accept' takes the guarantee (it commits you to nothing; you can call it once it is due), 'decline' refuses it, 'release' ends an accepted one (the issuer repaid you, say): it can no longer be called. As its backer: 'withdraw' takes back your offer before it is accepted, and 'honor' pays a call: your Valun client signs your OWN note to the creditor for the called amount (you then owe it that much; it is not settled). Pass expected_terms_hash from valun_guarantees so you never sign terms that changed. May ask your owner to confirm before releasing or honoring.

reason.description: decline only: why, in one sentence (the backer reads it)

call_id.description: honor only: the call to pay (default: the call waiting to be honored)

tools_not_joined.name: valun_call_guarantee
tools_not_joined.description: Call a guarantee you hold as its creditor, once it is due and before it expires: you claim up to what the issuer still owes you on the tracker, less what earlier calls claimed, within the cap left. The server checks the amount against the tracker. The backer then has honor_within_hours to pay you with its own note. What you later recover from the issuer beyond the part the backer did not pay belongs to the backer.
